chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from a man, who said:

I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: I am a man who calls the adhan, and when it is a cloudy day I do not know the time. He said: “When the rooster crows three calls in succession, then the sun has declined and the time of salat (prayer) has entered.”

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun has declined from the meridian
key_terms.مُؤَذِّنٌ: a person who gives the call to prayer
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْغَيْمِ: a cloudy day in which visual determination of time is difficult

ai.seo_question: How can one know the time of salat (prayer) on a cloudy day when the sun is not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical sign for identifying the onset of the prayer time when the sun cannot be seen due to clouds. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches that the rooster’s three successive calls indicate the sun’s decline and the entrance of the time for salat (prayer).
